On Fri, Jun 18, 2027 at 09:18 AM hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — triage note: I'm spinning up a short bridge. Initial look at metrics shows a sharp increase in token-generation latency and a concurrent autoscaler churn event.

Findings so far (short):
- 08:43:42 — first elevated token-latency sample; tail (95–99) increased from ~450ms to 3.2s for seq len > 800.
- 08:46:10 — Dedicated pool autoscaler registered node OOMs and removed 2 nodes; replacement provisioning created short capacity gap.
- 08:47:05 — We saw a brief routing fallback to a quantized model variant; many sessions reinitialised KV caches (cold KV rehydration).
- Error pattern: 502/503s consistent with kube proxy timeouts during node churn, not model generation failure.

I'll attach the request-level slices and host logs. Recommended immediate mitigation: pin traffic to a stable model variant, temporarily freeze autoscaler downscales for FR pool, and warm KV caches for longest sessions.

Attachments: tail-latency-samples.csv; host-logs-08-49.tar (stubs)

— Jonas
Sr. PM, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Interim readout and corrective plan — FastRetail outage follow-up

Emily / FastRetail ops team —

Thanks again for your patience. Quick interim readout: root cause appears to be a confluence of autoscaler node churn (OOM-driven) and an aggressive fallback to a quantized model variant that triggered widespread KV cache cold-starts. The node churn caused short-lived proxy timeouts which surfaced as 502/503 for user requests.

Immediate corrective actions we have applied:
- Pinned production routing to the verified full-precision model for the FastRetail pool (rollback enacted 2027-06-20 02:15 UTC).
- Disabled aggressive downscale for the FR Dedicated pool for 48 hours to prevent further capacity gaps.
- Pre-warmed KV caches for the top 2,000 active sessions.

Next steps and ownership:
- Formal RCA doc in draft (attached PDF). Owner: Jonas Weber — delivery target: 2027-06-24 EOD.
- Exec readout scheduled for 2027-06-25 14:00 PST. Hannah will present customer impact and closure plan; Laura to present operational mitigations and timeline.
- Follow-up: rollback hardening and autoscaler policy change ticket SUP-1338 (Jira link above).

We'll share a post-incident timeline and a list of preventive controls in the full RCA. Please let us know any specific evidence you need for your compliance/audit thread.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Chronicle closure register — final RCA delivery + commitments

Emily / FastRetail ops —

Attached is the final RCA (clean copy) and a compact closure register that records commitments, owners, deadlines, and verification steps. Highlights below: 

Summary:
- Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration allowed OOM-triggered node removals during a higher-than-expected memory allocation from a recent dependency update. The subsequent fallback to a quantized model caused extensive KV cold-starts; combined, these led to increased tail latency and proxy timeouts.

Key preventive measures (owners / timeline):
- Autoscaler policy change: set minimum available nodes to sustain 2x peak baseline; Owner: Kimberly Park; Due: 2027-07-02; Verification: load test + canary.
- Deploy-level memory safety checks: CI gate to reject sudden memory-taxing dependency bumps; Owner: Laura Bennett; Due: 2027-07-09; Verification: CI green with synthetic memory spike test.
- Routing policy enhancement: avoid automatic fallback to quantized variants for sessions > 600 tokens; Owner: Jonas Weber; Due: 2027-07-05; Verification: metric change and regression test.
- Compensation: Redwood will open a credits request with Sales for FastRetail — point person: Hannah Schmitt; Sales contact: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments included:
- 20270624-fastretail-final-rca.pdf
- closure-register-fastretail.csv
- tail-latency-samples.csv

Closure items will be tracked via SUP-1338 and weekly readouts until verified. If you'd like a separate compliance packet (PII check artifacts), say the word and we'll compile.

Thanks again for working through this with us. We consider the incident closed for customer-impact purposes pending the verification items above.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
